paragraphs.title: A Call to Thank the Lord with Joy

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.”
easy.q: Who is called to make a joyful noise unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Serve the LORD with gladness.”
easy.q: How are people instructed to serve the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “come before his presence with singing.”
easy.q: How should people come before the LORD’s presence?

answers: Both are connected with gladness and joyful worship
Only coming before Him is connected with joy
medium.explanation: The passage joins serving with gladness and coming before the LORD with singing.
medium.q: What connection is shown between serving the LORD and coming before His presence?

medium.explanation: “Gladness” describes joyful, cheerful service to the LORD.
medium.q: What does “gladness” mean in this passage?

answers: Make a joyful noise, serve with gladness, and come with singing
Come silently, leave quickly, and then serve
medium.explanation: These are the main actions commanded in the two verses.

answers: The call to worship is broad and universal
The call is meant for only one person
The call is meant only for shepherds
challenge.explanation: “All ye lands” shows that the invitation is not limited to a small group.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “all ye lands”?

challenge.explanation: Joyful noise, gladness, and singing all express joyful worship of the LORD.
challenge.q: What combination of attitudes is emphasized in these verses?

answers: To worship and honor the LORD
To distance oneself from the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verses call people to approach the LORD in joyful worship and praise.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of serving the LORD with gladness and singing before Him?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Know ye that the LORD he is God.”
easy.q: Who is God according to the verse?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves.”

answers: We are His people and the sheep of His pasture
We are strangers with no connection to Him
easy.explanation: The verse calls us “his people, and the sheep of his pasture.”
easy.q: How does the verse describe our relationship to the LORD?

answers: We recognize that we belong to Him
We conclude that we made Him
We conclude that we have no connection with Him
medium.explanation: The verse connects God’s creation of us with our identity as His people and flock.
medium.q: What follows from recognizing that the LORD made us?

answers: People under the LORD’s care and guidance
People who belong to no one
People who are fleeing from the shepherd
medium.explanation: The image of sheep in a pasture suggests care, guidance, and belonging.
medium.q: What does “the sheep of his pasture” suggest?

answers: Recognize God, recognize that He made us, and recognize that we belong to Him
Deny God, forget Him, and leave Him
medium.explanation: The verse moves from knowing who God is to recognizing His creation and ownership.
medium.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in the verse?

answers: Belonging to and being cared for by the LORD
Having no relationship with the LORD
challenge.explanation: Both descriptions express a relationship of belonging and care.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by “his people” and “the sheep of his pasture”?

answers: Because He is presented as our Creator and the One to whom we belong
Because there is no relationship between us
challenge.explanation: The verse presents God as the Maker of His people and describes them as belonging to Him.
challenge.q: Why is the statement that God made us connected with the statement that we are His?

answers: His people, and the sheep of his pasture
challenge.explanation: “His people” expresses communal belonging, while “the sheep of his pasture” suggests care and guidance.
challenge.q: Which phrase combines a communal relationship with an image of care and guidance?

paragraphs.title: Entering to Give Thanks and Bless

answers: Into his gates and into his courts
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Enter into his gates ... and into his courts.”
easy.q: Where are people invited to enter?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Enter into his gates with thanksgiving.”
easy.q: What should people bring when entering the LORD’s gates?

easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “be thankful unto him, and bless his name.”
easy.q: What should people do with the LORD’s name?

answers: Both are ways of honoring the LORD
One expresses anger and the other expresses fear
medium.explanation: The verse joins entering with thanksgiving and entering the courts with praise.
medium.q: What connection is shown between thanksgiving and praise?

answers: The enclosed areas connected with the LORD’s house
medium.explanation: In context, the courts are areas associated with the LORD’s house and worship.
medium.q: What does “courts” most likely refer to in this verse?

answers: Enter the gates, enter the courts, give thanks, and bless His name
Bless His name, leave, and then give thanks
Withdraw, remain silent, and then enter
medium.explanation: This follows the order of the commands in the verse.
medium.q: What is the order of instructions in the verse?

answers: As a broad call to thank the LORD and bless His name
As symbols of moving away from the LORD
challenge.explanation: Beyond a physical entrance, the language can express a general invitation to worship.
challenge.q: How may “gates” and “courts” be understood figuratively?

answers: From entering the holy place to thanksgiving, praise, and blessing
From thanksgiving to forgetting the LORD
challenge.explanation: Entering is presented together with thankful and praising worship.
challenge.q: What movement of thought occurs in this verse?

answers: Thankfulness to the LORD can be expressed in several ways
The verse concerns only physical entry
challenge.explanation: Thanksgiving, praise, thankfulness, and blessing all reinforce the theme of worship.
challenge.q: What does the use of several expressions of worship emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Goodness and Faithfulness Through Generations

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “For the LORD is good.”
easy.q: How does the verse describe the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “his mercy is everlasting.”
easy.q: How long is the LORD’s mercy?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “his truth endureth to all generations.”
easy.q: How long does the LORD’s truth endure?

answers: His everlasting mercy is an expression of His goodness
His mercy cancels out His goodness
medium.explanation: The verse presents the LORD as good and immediately describes His mercy as everlasting.
medium.q: What connection is made between the LORD’s goodness and His mercy?

medium.explanation: Here “truth” refers to the LORD’s enduring faithfulness.
medium.q: What does “truth” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD’s goodness, mercy, and enduring faithfulness
A command to turn away from the LORD
medium.explanation: The final verse summarizes the LORD’s goodness, everlasting mercy, and faithfulness.
medium.q: What central idea appears at the end of the psalm?

answers: “Everlasting” stresses endless duration, while “to all generations” stresses continuation across generations
“To all generations” means less than one day
challenge.explanation: Both expressions emphasize permanence, using different ways of describing it.
challenge.q: What distinction is suggested between “everlasting” and “to all generations”?

answers: It gives reasons for worship by describing the LORD’s goodness, mercy, and faithfulness
It removes the need to worship
It changes the subject to human accomplishments
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s enduring qualities provide a foundation for the earlier call to praise Him.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion strengthen the call to worship at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Both describe qualities of the LORD that endure over time
challenge.explanation: His mercy is everlasting, and His truth continues to all generations.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the LORD’s mercy and His truth?
